chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa'id, from his father, who said: I was with Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) when Dawud al-Raqqi entered upon him.

He said to him: May I be your ransom, the people say: When six months have passed for the pregnant woman, Allah has finished creating her. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: O Dawud, supplicate, even with a piece of the Safa. I said: May I be your ransom, and what is the Safa? He said: What is expelled with the child, for Allah does what He wills.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: The Safa (literally a smooth rock, here used metaphorically for the placenta or afterbirth)
key_terms.جَعَلْتُ فَدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a common honorific phrase used by Shia narrators)
key_terms.يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ: Does what He wills (emphasizing divine power)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Safa' in the context of fetal creation according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Ridha (AS) corrects the popular notion that fetal creation is complete at six months by linking the term 'Safa' (often associated with the stone in Mecca) to the placenta or afterbirth expelled with the child. This interpretation highlights the fluidity of divine creation, suggesting that while the fetus may appear formed, the process remains under Allah's direct will until the final expulsion. The hadith serves as a theological reminder against rigidly limiting divine power to specific biological timelines.

en.basel-kadem: 78.	With this chain of narrators, from Muhammed bin Ahmad, from Muhammed bin Harun, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, of the one he mentioned, that he said:

A man said to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him: People are saying: «The one who is not of Arab origin, nor a clearly declared mawla, is an inferior. He said: And what thing is a clearly declared mawla? The man said to him: The one who owns his parents. He said: And why did they say this? He said: They said it due to the saying of Allah’s Messenger, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family: A people’s mawla is from themselves. He said: Glory be to Allah, has it not reached you that the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: «I am the Master [1] of the one who has no master, and I am the Master of every Muslim, Arab and non-Arab»? Hence, the one who befriends the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, will he not be from the self of Allah’s Messenger, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family? He then said: Which of the two is more honored: the one who is from the self of Allah’s Messenger, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family; or the one who is from the self of an gross Arabian who urinates on his heels? Furthermore, he, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, said: The one who enters into Islam willingly is better than the one who enters out of fear. The hypocrites entered out of fear, whereas the mawali [2] entered willingly.
